title: A source marker separates reported from directly observed content
summary: Test whether a recurring whole marks information provenance, distinguishing a reported/source-derived field from a directly observed or performed field.

design.mechanism: The candidate scopes over a field's provenance and does not name the field's material or action.
design.unit: complete candidate occurrences in records with independently classified source/report status
design.contrast: candidate-bearing reported fields versus candidate-free direct-observation fields, matched by register and field position
design.prediction: Candidate-bearing contexts show a reproducible increase in source/report framing while local action and material roles remain unchanged; a lexical/content reading predicts no provenance interaction.
design.falsifier: No held provenance contrast after record controls, or the contrast follows one annotator's wording, falsifies the source-marker mechanism.
design.scope: cached records plus external source-status coding; endpoint availability_unknown
design.related: Different from modal obligation and genre interaction: provenance is source status, not command force or record type
